title: Selling a paid-off car when the title is lost
text: If you own your car outright and the paper title is lost or damaged, you need a duplicate title from your state before we can complete the purchase. We cannot buy a car that is fully paid off without a title. You can still get an offer and book an appointment while you wait. How long a duplicate takes depends on the state: [Virginia](kb:duplicate_title_virginia), [North Carolina](kb:duplicate_title_north_carolina), [Georgia](kb:duplicate_title_georgia), [Texas](kb:duplicate_title_texas), [California](kb:duplicate_title_california). If you still have a loan on the car, this article doesn't apply; see [Selling a car you are still paying off](kb:selling_with_loan).

title: Getting a duplicate title in Virginia
text: Virginia uses electronic titles, so there is usually no paper title to lose. If you need a printed copy, request a duplicate title online from the Virginia motor vehicle agency; it typically arrives in about a week. Bring the printout or the confirmation email to your appointment. See [States with electronic titles](kb:electronic_titles).

title: Getting a duplicate title in North Carolina
text: North Carolina issues paper titles. Request a duplicate by mail or at any North Carolina motor vehicle office, with your registration and a photo ID. Duplicates take 4 to 6 weeks to arrive. You can get an offer and book an appointment while you wait, but we can't complete the purchase until the duplicate arrives. Offers last a limited time, so you may need a new one ([How long is my offer good for?](kb:offer_validity)).

title: Getting a duplicate title in Georgia
text: Georgia issues paper titles. The duplicate title application must be signed by every owner on the title and notarized, then mailed or taken to a Georgia motor vehicle office. Duplicates take 2 to 3 weeks. You can get an offer and book an appointment while you wait. If an owner can't sign, see [When more than one person owns the car](kb:co_owners).

title: Getting a duplicate title in Texas
text: Texas uses electronic titles. If you need a printed duplicate, request it online from the Texas motor vehicle agency; it arrives in 5 to 7 business days. For a sale to Northwind you usually don't need the printout, because we transfer the electronic title at the appointment ([States with electronic titles](kb:electronic_titles)).

title: Getting a duplicate title in California
text: California issues paper titles. Apply for a duplicate at any California motor vehicle office with your photo ID and registration. The main offices print duplicates the same day; by mail, it takes 2 to 3 weeks. Bring the duplicate to your appointment.

title: Salvage and rebuilt titles
text: A branded title shows that a car was declared a total loss, and possibly rebuilt afterward. Northwind doesn't buy cars with salvage, rebuilt or flood titles. If your title is branded, we're unable to make an offer. See [Flood-damaged cars](kb:flood_damage).

title: Salvage and rebuilt titles
text: A branded title shows that a car was declared a total loss, and possibly rebuilt afterward. We now buy cars with rebuilt titles, at a reduced offer that reflects the brand; the specialist confirms the amount at the appraisal. We still don't buy cars with salvage titles or flood titles ([Flood-damaged cars](kb:flood_damage)). Select the title brand when you request an offer: an offer made for a clean title will change at the appraisal if the title turns out to be branded ([What can change your offer](kb:what_changes_offer)).

title: The name on the title doesn't match my ID
text: If the name on the title doesn't match your photo ID, for example after marriage or a legal name change, bring the document that shows the change: a marriage certificate, divorce decree or court order. You also sign the name change affidavit, form NW-NMC-1, at the appointment. If the title has a spelling mistake, ask your state's motor vehicle agency to correct it first. If an ex-spouse is still listed as an owner, see [My ex is still on the title](kb:divorce_ex_on_title).

title: States with electronic titles
text: Virginia and Texas use electronic titles: the title is a record at the state, not a paper document. When you sell a car with an electronic title, there's no paper title to bring; we transfer the title electronically at the appointment. If there was a loan, the lender releases the lien electronically too ([My loan is paid off but the lien is still on the title](kb:lien_still_on_title)). North Carolina, Georgia and California use paper titles.
